utterances.text: The Bravo Company and the PTT buildings. That's what I mainly walked, and they are not very far apart, couple hundred yards maybe. However, my stay, where I was residing in those days, was at Bravo.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: For how many hours would you say you were in Srebrenica that day?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Do you recall where the petrol station was in relation to Bravo Company?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd have to see images of it. But if this was a location at which there used to be a bus stop, where you could get on the bus, then I do have that image, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, assuming it's there, how far?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe a hundred, 200 metres. However, I believe that for a clear image one should see a picture. Otherwise it's going to be too vague for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm not going to argue with that, Colonel Boering. What I'd now like to you do is have a look at a video which has been played to this Chamber before but not to you. It's V00-4417, also known as 4 D14. Perhaps that could be played.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Is that the petrol station that you had in mind in relation to the questions I just asked you?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I am told that the images depicted in that video occurred on the 10th of July of 1995. Did you see anything like that whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think we can have the break now and then Mr. Sarapa will start his cross-examination afterwards. 25 minutes, please. I beg your pardon. It's 30 minutes, not 25 minutes, and that's because of the redaction. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sarapa. Do you think you can finish in 45 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best. My predecessors have covered a lot of questions that I intended to ask, so I sincerely hope that I'll be able to finish within that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a classic case of great minds think alike.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for those words.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Colonel, sir, I would like to ask you some personal questions, not personal as such but some related to your career. When you spoke about your military career, you have provided us with some detail of the offices that you held before arrival in Srebrenica. Can you please repeat that? Can you provide us with some more detail as to what you did before arriving in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the military academy from 1987 to 1982 [as interpreted]. Then I became lieutenant, and after that, from 1982 to 1989, I served in Germany with artillery. During that time I was involved in manoeuvring units as a sort of liaison person. Infantry, reconnaissance unit. After that, for six months, I took leave. I wasn't in the army. So we can skip that. Then I joined the army in the artillery centre in Breda, where I was for one year. From then, I did a course in The Hague, and then for two and two and a half years I was placed in the Ministry of Defence in The Hague, with the procurement of material was one of my tasks. And following on from that, I went back to Seedorf in the brigade where I was an artillery officer. And following on from that, after one year, there was talk that I be sent to the Dutch patrol, so I went from the brigade staff and I became seconded to Assen, and I was in the programme with some other external people in order to reinforce them. I was there for about two, three months, where I was involved in preparation and then I was detached or sent. That's it in brief. I was sent on missions after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: During your stay in Srebrenica, during your mission, did you have the right of command?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You don't have it as a staff officer. I played a more coordinating role, and I played an advising -- advisory role.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please play 7 D00028? Very well. This document is in B/C/S. It was found rather late. We did not have the time to translate it. So I would like the interpreters to interpret what I'm going to read. This is a document by the BiH army, by the command of the 8th Operations Group Srebrenica, the security sector. The number is 130503 and the date is 11 January 1995, in Srebrenica, and it is delivered to the security sector of the -- security organ of the 2nd Corps in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May it be noted that the interpreters do not have that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No one has it on the main screen. It appears now. You should have it now. Please confirm to me if you don't.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: This is the beginning: "Due to the enemy attack to take Ravni Buljim, TT 820, and due to the fact that the UNPROFOR did not agree to place an observation at that place, the command of the 8th OG Srebrenica has banned the UNPROFOR members to approach the area and to reinforce the Buljim-Jabucno line." And later on there is another part of the text. "The 8th OG Srebrenica has given an ultimatum to the members of the United Nations and asked them to return the enemy soldiers to their initial positions. Should they not comply with that condition, the command will forbid the movement by the UNPROFOR in this zone." Colonel, sir, could you please tell us whether you have any information about this document? The date is 11 January 1995, and this was the time when you were already there.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's be clear, because you never know in this place. The question that you asked is whether he knows anything about this document, whether you have any information about this document. And he --

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And he has answered that he hasn't. Perhaps if we could rephrase the question to make sure that what you meant to elicit from the witness is whether he can tell us anything about the contents of this document that you read out to him. In other words about --

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Colonel, this is not a question as to whether you've seen this document before or whether you know anything about it. It's a question of whether you know anything about the facts or the events that it refers to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can recall that there were talks about the number of observation posts around the enclave. I didn't carry them out myself, but Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans did. In the beginning, I wasn't the military LO yet, but I do remember there were talks about the need or the desirability to have other locations for observation posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is precisely what I meant. I wanted to discuss the contents of the document, not the document itself. And now I would kindly ask for 7 D0030 to be put on the screen. Yes. We have it on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: This is a document by the General Staff of the army, the army staff, Kakanj, 29 January 1995. And it was sent to the command of the 8th OG Srebrenica. It was signed by the Chief of Staff, General Enver Hadzihasanovic. At the beginning of the document, it says: "The UNPROFOR in your zone has very well defined tasks that they are supposed to follow. In conversations with the liaison officer of the UNPROFOR, make sure that the UNPROFOR complies with their commitments. Do not allow them to go to possible new observation points." My question to you is this: Do you know who the liaison officer was at the time? And I'm referring to the 29th of January, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a short document and we don't have it in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but the question is whether he knows who was the LO at this time, January 1995. I don't even know whether he had arrived then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, under the old rules as I remember them, the appropriate question would be that question, without a document. There is no reason to refresh his recollection or impeach him. He just can ask him: Do you know who the LO was? And there is no reason for a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we have advanced 13 years since this Tribunal started. You know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If you think that's an advance. These documents, and reading them is taking quite a bit of time. I think there were some reasons for those old rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're 100 per cent right, Mr. McCloskey, but let's proceed with the question because that's what we really should be concentrating upon. You're being asked, Colonel, whether you know who the liaison officer was in January, end of January of 1995. If you can answer that question, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether it was the LO that was intended in this letter, but I had a colleague, and together we had prepared some discussion points. I can't recall that we discussed something as appears in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That answer is more than you bargained for, Mr. Sarapa. So let's proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now have 7 D00026 on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, we don't seem to have a translation of this document into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It exists only in B/C/S, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have an impression of having seen this document already during the proceedings. No, but that referred to June or July. No. No. This is February.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we have the right document on the screen. The previous one was a wrong one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: This is a document of the BIH army, the command of the 28th Division. The number is 01-17/95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go to the question, Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: I'm going to read one part of the document and then I'll put my question to the witness. "On 27 April 1995, the command of the DutchBat of UNPROFOR in Srebrenica started to reinforce -- to reinforce their lines in order to set up an observation point in the sector of Lozina village. This will allow for the control of the corridor between Srebrenica and Zepa, and this will directly have an impact on the security and the confidentiality of the transport of MTS which is delivered to Srebrenica in this way. The liaison officer of the 28th Division of the Srebrenica army asked for an urgent meeting with the representatives of the DutchBat, and he met with them on two occasions, the first time on the 28th of April, 1995, at 10.00 and at 1600 hours." Colonel, sir, do you know anything about these particular meetings?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember the subject matter, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Did you attend either both of these meetings or at least one of them?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not quite clear in my memory. What I do recall is that we have discussed whether or not to establish an additional observation post. That is something that I do remember. However, whether that took place in this precise period is something that is possible. It certainly does connect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have number 7 D00036 on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document, again, a document by the army of Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the date is 29 April 1995, sent to the command of the 28th Division. This is an order which reads: "The command of the 28th Division of the army in cooperation with the civilian structures of Srebrenica municipality should take all measures and prevent further works leading towards the setting up of an observation point of the UNPROFOR in the Lozina village sector." Under 3 it says: "The civilian organs of authorities have to get in touch with the Dutch Battalion and they should be provided with some instructions, and the SJB has to provide physical security to the axis where the works are taking place." Colonel, sir, are you familiar with this event? Do you know what transpired after this? Especially what about the provision of physical security at the place where the works are taking place?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot remember anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 7 D00034 on the screen, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: The date on the document is 29 April 1995. It was sent to the command of the 28th Division and to the command of the 2nd Corps. It says: "In your document, we received order regarding the observation point of the UN in the sector of Lozina on the corridor of the demilitarised zone, Srebrenica-Zepa. At 10.00 on the same day the representatives of the command of the 28th Division and the civilian authorities held a meeting with the representatives of the UN and military observers." My question to you is this: Do you know who military observers were?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that these were the United Nations military observers present in the enclave. These were about four individuals and they would take turns in carrying out their work. There was a Major Kingori, Major de Haan, and there were several other observers. However, their names are not quite clear to me at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Would you be able to remember the names of the UN liaison officers?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the names of the UNMOs. I just gave you two names. As to liaison officers, well, at that point, that was me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. My next question is whether you attended this meeting. Do you remember having attended this meeting?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I did. It's possible that either Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans or Commander Franken, or Lieutenant Franken organised a meeting themselves, in presence of the company commander as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Colonel, sir, do you remember whether you attended any meetings that were held with the representatives of the Muslim army that had to do with the observation points? Apparently there was a problem, and I suppose these were not the only meetings. These are the only documents that I have at my disposal. However, I assume there were other meetings, and my question to you is whether you attended any other meetings of the kind of -- on any other days, at any other times.

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: During meetings with the ABiH, the issue of observation posts was mentioned regularly. The matter was discussed whether posts should or could be removed, whether there were positions in the right way. These matters were discussed. However, I haven't been involved in this personally, and when this issue would be raised, it would be on the competence of either Lieutenant-Colonel Karremans or Mr. Franken. I never dealt with these matters myself. And whenever there were meetings dealing with this issue, then whenever possible, I would not participate in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at document 7 D00041, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Document of the 29th of April, 1995, sent by the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the command of the 2nd Corps in Tuzla, the 28th Division. Item 1 states: "UNPROFOR's claim is correct in Srebrenica that the same de jure has an unlimited freedom of movement and selection of locations for observation posts, in the territory of Srebrenica. Agreement on the demilitarisation of Srebrenica and Zepa dated 8th May 1993. "Item 2: UNPROFOR's claim is correct that based on the agreement on the demilitarisation, they are obliged to prevent any attempt of entry by uniformed persons, military equipment and combat vehicles to the demilitarised zone. In view of the above and understanding the possible serious consequences of setting up UNPROFOR observation posts, as far as the army of Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina is concerned, i.e., the jeopardy of the corridor for Zepa, we suggest the following: The subject problem should not be raised at the level of the GSA, BH command of UNPROFOR, because the UNPROFOR unit in Srebrenica would in that way have enough time to set up the command post -- the observation posts." My question is as follows: It transpires clearly on the basis of this that the objective was to gain time. You, Colonel, were you familiar, and you confirmed that earlier, that you knew about the problem of the observation posts and were you aware at the time that the actions of the military authorities of the B and H army were actually intended to drag things out?

utterances.speaker: PIETER BOERING [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I take a very deep look in my memories, then I can affirm that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move into private session now, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move into private session. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Colonel, we have to end here today. Unfortunately, you haven't finished. We require 15 minutes minimum, or a little bit more than that, depending on whether there is going to be re-examination tomorrow. And then you're free to go. But your presence is required again, unfortunately. So I wish to thank you for bearing with us, and have a nice evening, and I'll see you again -- we'll see you again tomorrow afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 27th day of September, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
